claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has high strength but limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries create local stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
The local stress concentrations caused by dislocation pile-ups promote premature microcracking and catastrophic damage during straining.
Post-solidification annealing followed by rapid quenching can produce fine secondary precipitates at internal phase boundaries within the lamellar colonies.
The proposed secondary precipitates will be ductile.
The precipitates will act as dislocation sinks or diffusion zones.
The precipitates will interrupt continuous dislocation pile-ups and disperse local strain.
Interrupting dislocation pile-ups and dispersing strain will alleviate stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
Alleviating boundary stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation.
The treatment will increase elongation at failure relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will delay or reduce catastrophic crack propagation relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Refined microstructural features associated with the treatment can provide strength retention or enhancement.
The proposed effect is intended to apply primarily during room-temperature tensile loading under ambient conditions.
Treatment effectiveness may depend on alloy composition and microstructural scale.
Inappropriate annealing conditions could coarsen the phases or weaken the interfaces.
